name: missing-app

error.messageIncludes: app must be a non-empty string.

note: captured from a real run: parseModelAction on this input throws 'app must be a non-empty string.'. The `app` read fires first — src/lib/actionValidation.ts:54 runs readFirstString(candidate, ['app']) before the packageName check at :56 — so the bad packageName in this input is never diagnosed. This fixture pins that ordering on purpose: the package-name rejection itself is asserted by invalid-package.json, which supplies "app":"Chrome". A model reply that names a bad package but omits `app` therefore gets the misleading `app` diagnostic; if the validation order is ever reversed, this fixture fails.
